newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran police seizes 486 kg of drugs.
newsitem.headline: Iran police seizes 486 kg of drugs.

text.p: Iran has seized half a tonne of drugs in an armed clash with traffickers in the southeast of the country, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported on Saturday.

IRNA quoted law enforcement officials as saying police seized on Friday 486 kg (1,071 lb) of a substance it described as "morphine" after a gunbattle in the town of Saravan near the border with Pakistan.
It said rocket launchers and assault rifles were used in the clash. IRNA gave no details on casualties but said the smugglers fled.
In another operation, law enforcement forces seized 42 kg (92.5 lb) of illegal drugs including 2.8 kg (6.1 lb) of opium, the agency added.

According to Iranian law, possession of five kg (11 lb) of opium or 30 grammes (just over one ounce) of heroine is punishable by death. More than 1,000 people have been executed in drug-related cases since the law took effect in 1989.
Iran is a key transit route for drugs, mostly opium from which heroine is made, being smuggled to Europe via Turkey from Afghanistan and Pakistan.
